summary: Singles' Day ends with sales up 4.8%, about a third of last year's growth, as AI shopping tools spread faster than shoppers' budgets.
body: China's Singles' Day shopping season ended on Nov 11. Data firm Syntun estimates sales rose 4.8% from a year earlier to 1.78 trillion yuan (about $267 billion US) over the period from Oct 7 to Nov 11, Reuters reports. Last year's festival grew 14.2%.[^1] Reuters points to low consumer confidence, the long fall in property prices, weak income expectations and worries about jobs.[^1] Alibaba and JD.com no longer publish their total sales, so outside estimates like Syntun's are the main measure.[^1]

AI was the main new feature. JD.com says it sold more than 50 million AI-related products, sales of AI PCs, glasses and cameras more than doubled, and sales of "token" packages, prepaid units for using AI models, rose more than tenfold.[^1] Chatbots that recommend and buy products were widely used, but it is unclear how much extra spending they caused.[^1] A Beijing analyst says the festival is "not as lively as it used to be" because discounts now run all year.[^1]

My read: Chinese shoppers are buying new gadgets, but carefully, and a weak home market is one reason Chinese companies keep pushing exports. Next week, the APEC summit in Shenzhen brings Xi Jinping together with leaders including Canada's Mark Carney, and US officials plan to start a dialogue with China on advanced AI there.[^2][^3]
